groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 68.60 listing.

groups.statement: Layered and confined nanoscale systems are structures built from stacked films or from quantum confinement in one, two, or three dimensions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS 68.65 listing of layered and confined systems.

groups.statement: Low-dimensional carbon and wire-like nanostructures are nanoscale systems whose confined geometry is a wire or a single atomic sheet.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from quantum wires to graphene films.

groups.statement: Electronic-structure sections and many-electron models are theoretical frameworks for describing electrons in bulk condensed matter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from broad sections down to specific models.

groups.statement: Models of interacting many-electron systems, from the uniform electron gas to fermions hopping on a lattice, whose scale is set by ħ and the electron number N rather than by c or G.
Model-system and excited-state topics treat interacting many-electron physics where ħ and the particle number N set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Next degree: ħ and N govern correlation among many particles.

groups.statement: First-principles computational methods are non-relativistic schemes whose scale is set by ħ and the number of electrons N.
groups.rank_note: Methods: ħ and N govern, c absent.

groups.statement: Band-structure studies of metals and alloys have scales set by ħ and N, with c and G playing no role.
groups.rank_note: Materials: ħ and N only.

groups.statement: Band-structure studies of semiconductors and other compounds have scales set by ħ and N, with c and G playing no role.
groups.rank_note: Materials: ħ and N only.

groups.statement: Computational methods for electronic structure calculations are classified by the numerical techniques and basis representations used to solve the many-electron problem, with the scale of each claim set by ħ and the electron number N.
Disordered solids are materials whose electronic structure lacks long-range periodic order, including amorphous and quasicrystalline systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general theory to specific disordered materials.

groups.statement: Collective and molecular-solid topics cover fullerene materials and plasmon-type collective response functions of electrons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from molecular solids to collective response.

groups.statement: Basic exciton topics cover bound electron-hole pairs in their general, self-trapped, intrinsic, plasma and interaction forms.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general exciton phenomena to specific forms.

groups.statement: Field-dependent and many-body exciton topics cover magnetoexcitons, collective excitonic effects and charged excitons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from field effects to collective and charged complexes.

groups.statement: Polarons are carriers dressed by electron-phonon interaction, ranging from mass renormalization to large, small and paired polarons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general electron-phonon coupling to specific polaron types.

groups.statement: Electronic-structure topics covering collective charge ordering and the general impurity and defect levels heading.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 71 hierarchy.

groups.statement: Impurity and defect levels classified by the kind of host material in which the impurity sits.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 71.55 list of host materials.

groups.statement: Level splitting caused by the crystal lattice environment, through crystal fields or strain.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 71.70 list.

groups.statement: Level splitting and interactions driven by magnetic fields, spin and orbital coupling, exchange and nuclear effects.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 71.70 list.

groups.statement: Electronic transport theory and the scattering mechanisms that limit conduction, including scattering from disordered structures.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by position in the PACS 72 hierarchy.

groups.statement: Electrical conduction in condensed matter is divided into two top-level headings: conduction in metals and alloys, and conductivity phenomena in semiconductors and insulators.
groups.rank_note: General headings for metals and for semiconductors and insulators.

groups.statement: Conduction is divided by the structural order of the material and by the theory and transport regime that governs carrier motion in it.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from amorphous to crystalline structure, then general theory and mobility edges.

groups.statement: Magnetotransport and thermoelectric effects are the responses of conducting materials to magnetic fields and temperature gradients.
groups.rank_note: Metals first, then semiconductors, pairing each effect type.

groups.statement: Scattering, relaxation, collective and localization phenomena describe how carriers lose momentum, relax, or become confined during conduction.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from relaxation and collective modes through scattering to localization and carrier dynamics.

groups.statement: Field-driven and spin-dependent transport covers nonlinear carrier behavior and the flow of spin-polarized currents in metals and semiconductors.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from carrier generation and high-field effects to spin-polarized transport.

groups.statement: Spin injection processes are the ways spin-polarized carriers are created, by light or by electrical current.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Spin transport and loss processes govern how spin moves across interfaces, is pumped by current, and decays by scattering.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Conventional and inorganic conducting materials are crystalline semiconductors, transition-metal compounds and insulators studied for their conductivity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Soft, disordered and nanostructured conducting materials include polymers, glasses, liquids, fullerenes, composites and graphene.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Surface, interface and general conductivity headings frame the electronic structure and methods that apply across low-dimensional systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Surface electronic states and their band-structure properties are kinds of single-particle surface descriptions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from band states to defect-bound levels.

groups.statement: Localization and delocalization are opposing kinds of disorder-driven behavior of electrons at surfaces.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, localization followed by its opposite.

groups.statement: Low-dimensional layered and confined structures are kinds of engineered systems classified by their geometry of electron confinement.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from layered stacks to confinement in two, one and zero dimensions.

groups.statement: Nanoscale and mesoscopic electronic systems are kinds of small-scale systems studied through their electronic states and transport.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from nanoscale electronic structure to mesoscopic transport.

groups.statement: The group covers Collective excitations and Broken symmetry phases as one kind of claim.
Quantum-coherent and quantized transport topics have scales set by ħ and the conductance quantum, with channel number N counting the modes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the topic, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Tunneling topics have scales set by ħ through barrier transmission, with the number of conducting channels N sets the total current.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the topic, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Contact and general interface transport topics have scales set by contact resistance and potential, where the number of channels N in the contact sets the Sharvin-type resistance.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the topic, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Semiconductor junction and rectifying topics have scales set by classical band-bending and depletion physics, with ħ entering only weakly.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the topic, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Layered heterostructure topics have scales set by layer sequence and band offsets, with the number of layers N and no relativistic constant c or G involved.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the topic, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Quantum-coherent magnetotransport phenomena are those in which Planck's constant sets the scale of the response of electrons to a magnetic field.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from transitions to resistance effects.

groups.statement: General transport theory covers the overarching framework and scattering mechanisms that govern how charge carriers move in thin films.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the film heading to general theory.

groups.statement: Drive-dependent transport covers how film conduction responds to the strength and frequency of applied electric fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from low-field to high-field to high-frequency.

groups.statement: Carrier dynamics and coupled transport effects cover how carriers are generated and lost, and how their flow couples to magnetic, thermal, optical, acoustic and noise phenomena.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from carrier lifetime to coupled effects to noise.

groups.statement: Electrical properties of specific thin-film materials are grouped by the class of material, such as metals, semiconductors and glasses.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general heading to metals to semiconductor classes.

groups.statement: Bulk and molecular materials are condensed matter systems whose electronic properties are set by the many-electron count N.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Nanoscale structures are systems confined in one or more dimensions, where ħ and the confinement length set the scale of electronic transport.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Microscopic theories of superconductivity explain the pairing mechanism and symmetry from quantum mechanics, with ħ and the pairing energy setting the scale.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Phenomenological and thermodynamic descriptions treat superconductors through macroscopic, ensemble-level models and measured properties.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Claims about electronic transport in nanoscale materials and nanotubes, whose scale is set by the quantum of conductance (ħ and the electron charge) and by the small number N of conducting channels.
Transport and thermal response covers how charge and heat flow through a superconductor.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general transport to its electric, thermal and thermoelectric forms.

groups.statement: Electromagnetic response and spectroscopy covers how a superconductor reacts to and is probed by light, radio-frequency fields and nuclear spins.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general electromagnetic response to specific optical and resonance probes.

groups.statement: Vortex and magnetic phenomena covers how a superconductor responds to magnetic fields and carries current through the mixed state.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from magnetic properties through the mixed state and vortex phases to pinning and critical currents.

groups.statement: Lattice and electronic structure covers the electronic states, lattice vibrations and mechanical behavior of the superconducting solid.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from electronic states to phonons and then elastic behavior.

groups.statement: Phase behavior and fluctuations covers the phase boundaries of superconductivity and the random or nonequilibrium departures from the ordered state.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the phase diagram to fluctuations, noise and nonequilibrium states.

groups.statement: Simple and multi-element inorganic compounds form non-cuprate superconductors defined by their chemical composition.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 74.70 listing.

groups.statement: Superconductors built from molecular, carbon, ruthenium oxide or strongly correlated heavy-fermion materials form an exotic non-cuprate family.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 74.70 listing.

groups.statement: Cuprate superconductors are distinguished by the doping type or electronic state of the copper-oxide material.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 74.72 listing.

groups.statement: Factors that change the superconducting transition temperature include synthesis, composition, doping and disorder.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 74.62 listing.

groups.statement: Pressure, quantum criticality, the pseudogap and other external or collective tuning effects form a distinct kind of influence on superconductivity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Superconducting films and low-dimensional structures are superconductors whose reduced geometry, layering, or nanoscale size shapes their behavior.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general low-dimensional category to specific structure types.

groups.statement: Inhomogeneous superconducting systems are superconductors whose granular, amorphous, composite, or networked makeup makes their properties spatially non-uniform.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general inhomogeneous category to specific types.

groups.statement: General theories and models of magnetic ordering are the theoretical frameworks, including spin Hamiltonians and spin models, used to describe magnetism.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general theory category to specific model types.

groups.statement: Exotic and itinerant magnetic models cover quantum spin liquids, band models, random spin systems, and chain models, along with a method for open quantum dynamics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from quantum phases to itinerant, random, and chain models, then the dynamics method.

groups.statement: Diamagnetism, paramagnetism, and local-moment phenomena are magnetic responses of materials, classified by whether the material is a nonmetal, a metal, or a Kondo or heavy-fermion system.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general category to nonmetals, metals, then local-moment compounds.

groups.statement: Ordering and arrangement topics concern how spins, orbitals and charges are arranged in magnetically ordered materials, including density-wave states.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general spin arrangements to orbital and charge orders and spin-density waves.

groups.statement: Interaction and excitation topics concern the couplings between magnetic moments and the collective or impurity-driven excitations that result from them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from basic exchange couplings to excitations and impurity or heavy-fermion interactions.

groups.statement: Bulk response topics concern intrinsic measurable properties of a magnetic material such as moments, anisotropy, phase boundaries and the magnetocaloric effect.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from intrinsic materials properties to phase boundaries and thermal response.

groups.statement: Critical-point topics concern behavior near magnetic transitions, covering static and dynamic properties and numerical simulation studies.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general critical-point heading to static, dynamic and simulation approaches.

groups.statement: Magnetotransport topics concern changes in electrical resistance of materials caused by magnetic fields, including giant and colossal magnetoresistance.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general heading to the specific giant and colossal magnetoresistance effects.

groups.statement: Metallic ferromagnets are magnetic materials whose magnetism comes from metals such as iron and their alloys.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: iron-based alloys first, then other ferromagnetic metals and alloys, then the general metals and alloys category.

groups.statement: Oxide, nonmetallic and semiconducting magnets are magnetic materials that are not simple metals, including oxides, insulating ferromagnets and magnetic semiconductors.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: oxides, then nonmetallic ferromagnets, then magnetic semiconductors, then other materials.

groups.statement: Ordered and disordered spin-arrangement magnets are materials classified by how their atomic moments align or fail to align, including antiferromagnets, ferrimagnets, amorphous magnets and spin glasses.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: antiparallel ordering first, then ferrimagnetic ordering, then amorphous and random arrangements.

groups.statement: Application-oriented and small-scale magnetic materials are classed by their physical form or intended use, such as liquids, recording media, fine particles, permanent magnets and molecular magnets.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: fluid and recording forms, then particles, then hard magnets, then molecular magnets.

groups.statement: Domain-level and general magnetic phenomena cover the overall study of specific magnetic materials and the domain, magnetization-curve and hysteresis effects they show.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: the general materials heading first, then domain effects, then domain walls.

groups.statement: Hysteresis and reversal phenomena describe how a bulk magnet's magnetization responds to applied fields and thermal history over time.
Film and interface magnetism covers magnetic properties that arise from reduced dimensionality and from the boundaries of a layered material.
Domain and spin-orbit effects in films concern the internal magnetic structure and relativistic coupling that shape thin-film magnetic order.
Magnetic nanostructures are small-scale magnetic objects characterized by how they are made, how their domains are arranged, and how their electrons and moments behave.
Magnetization dynamics and resonance treat the time-dependent motion of magnetic moments, from simulation to ultrafast switching and resonance spectroscopy.
EPR of paramagnetic ions and impurities is divided by the type of ion, from the general case through the iron, palladium-platinum, rare-earth and other groups.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the general heading to specific ion families.

groups.statement: EPR of non-ionic paramagnetic centres covers defects, conduction electrons and free radicals as sources of unpaired spins.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally by type of spin source.

groups.statement: NMR spectral and relaxation observables describe how nuclear resonance lines shift, relax or split in the sample.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the parent heading to specific observables.

groups.statement: NMR field effects, echo methods and imaging cover internal fields, spin echoes and image formation from nuclear resonance.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally by method.

groups.statement: Double resonance techniques combine two magnetic or optical resonances so that one spin system is detected or polarized through another.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from the parent heading to specific techniques.

groups.statement: Bulk dielectric properties describe how solids and liquids respond to an applied electric field through permittivity, polarization and loss.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the whole field to its specific response properties.

groups.statement: Breakdown and film-structure topics cover the failure limit of dielectrics and the general and epitaxial organization of dielectric thin films.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from breakdown to general films to epitaxial layered films.

groups.statement: Films classified by permittivity level or target electronics are distinguished by the role they play in devices.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from permittivity-defined films to electronics-platform-defined films.

groups.statement: Functional dielectric films are distinguished by the electromechanical, thermal, magnetic or paraelectric response they exhibit.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in the PACS scheme.

groups.statement: Material-specific films are defined by their oxide chemistry, namely titanate, zirconate-titanate and niobate or tantalate compounds.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in the PACS scheme.

groups.statement: Thin-film piezoelectric and ferroelectric materials are classed by the specific compound that forms the film.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 77.55 listing, from ferroelectric films through named compounds to other piezoelectric films.

groups.statement: Piezoelectric and electromechanical effects are the coupling of mechanical strain and electric polarization, classed by the kind of effect or quantity observed.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 77.65 listing, from general effects through constants, surface waves, resonance and strain-induced fields.

groups.statement: Ferroelectric phenomena are the collective behaviors of spontaneous polarization, such as phase transitions, domains and switching.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 77.80 listing, from general ferroelectricity to transitions, domains, switching and relaxors.

groups.statement: Extrinsic influences on ferroelectric behavior are the composition, size scaling and strain or interface conditions that modify the material's response.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 77.80 sub-listing of compositional, scaling and strain effects.

groups.statement: Dielectric, piezoelectric and ferroelectric bulk materials are classed by their chemical type, such as elements, oxides and nitrides.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 77.84 listing, from the general heading to the specific chemical classes.

groups.statement: Inorganic ferroelectric crystals and ceramics are rigid crystalline dielectric materials whose lattice structure produces piezoelectric and ferroelectric behavior.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from perovskite ceramics to niobates to hydrogen-bonded crystals.

groups.statement: Soft and composite dielectric materials are organic, fluid or mixed-phase media whose polarization response comes from molecular or multiphase structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from polymers to composites to liquids.

groups.statement: Fundamental optical characterization covers the theory and the basic measurable optical properties of a material such as constants, activity and birefringence.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from theory to measured constants to polarization-dependent properties.

groups.statement: Field-induced optical effects are changes in a material's optical response caused by an applied electric, magnetic, light-induced or thermal stimulus.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from electric to magnetic to light-driven to thermal stimulus.

groups.statement: Mechanical and acoustic optical coupling comprises the top-level headings and the effects where strain, sound or ultrasound interacts with light in condensed matter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the overarching headings down to specific acoustic-optic effects.

groups.statement: Photothermal-family effects are optical phenomena in which absorbed light is converted into heat or thermal signals that are then detected.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Infrared and Raman spectra of crystalline semiconductors, insulators, metals and alloys probe the vibrational response of ordered solids.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Infrared and Raman spectra of nonmetallic, organic, disordered and carbon-cage solids cover materials that are not simple crystalline elements or metals.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Infrared and Raman spectra of liquids are classified by the chemical nature of the liquid, whether organic, inorganic or a solution.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Visible and ultraviolet absorption and reflection spectra are classified by the type of material measured, from liquids to metals.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing.

groups.statement: Optical studies of solids are organized by the class of material examined, such as organic, disordered or fullerene systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from molecular materials to disordered solids to carbon cage materials.

groups.statement: Spectroscopy of solid state dynamics is classified by the time-scale regime and resolution at which dynamics are measured.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by time resolution, from the general field to picosecond-scale to sub-picosecond ultrafast to high-resolution nonlinear methods.

groups.statement: Time-resolved studies are classified by the kind of excitation or species whose dynamics are probed.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from excited states to conduction electrons to radicals.

groups.statement: Time-resolved optical techniques are classified by the measured signal, whether absorption, luminescence, scattering or reflection.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the type of optical signal detected.

groups.statement: Coherent transient and nonlinear phenomena are those in which phase-coherent optical responses of the solid are observed in time.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general coherent spectroscopy to specific coherent effects.

groups.statement: Nonlinear laser spectroscopies probe the coherent optical response of a material using multiple laser fields.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in PACS 78.47.

groups.statement: Photoluminescence of crystalline semiconductors and solid inorganic materials is classified by the type of crystal that emits.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in PACS 78.55.

groups.statement: Photoluminescence of liquids, organic solids, porous solids and disordered solids covers emitters that are not simple crystals, together with the general heading.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in PACS 78.55.

groups.statement: Non-optically excited luminescence is light emission driven by electric fields, particle beams, heat, stimulation light or mechanical action.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as listed in PACS 78.60.

groups.statement: Sonoluminescence, triboluminescence and thermoluminescence are luminescence phenomena in which light emission is triggered by mechanical, acoustic or thermal energy rather than by optical or electrical excitation.
Chemiluminescence and the general heading for thin-film optics frame the field, one being light emission from chemical reactions and the other the umbrella class for thin-film optical properties.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: the emission process first, then the general thin-film heading.

groups.statement: Inorganic crystalline and metallic thin films are films of metals, elemental semiconductors and compound semiconductors whose optical properties are studied.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: metals, then elemental, III-V, II-VI and other semiconductors.

groups.statement: Disordered, insulating and organic thin films are non-crystalline or insulating film materials such as glasses, insulators, polymers and organic compounds.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: amorphous, insulating, then organic films.

groups.statement: Low-dimensional and nanoscale structures are objects confined in one or more dimensions, from the general class through particles, tubes, wells, dots and wires to engineered multilayers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: general class, then nanoparticles, tubes, wells, dots, wires, and multilayered structures.

groups.statement: Nanotubes and quantum wires are one-dimensional nanostructures whose optical properties are set by quantum confinement, so the scale of such claims is governed by ħ together with the particle number N rather than by c or G.
Elongated and composite nanostructures are materials whose optical properties are set by their rod, wire, porous or aggregated geometry.
groups.rank_note: n/a

groups.statement: Liquid-based nanostructures are droplet and micelle systems whose optical properties arise from their self-assembled fluid form.
groups.rank_note: n/a

groups.statement: X-ray interaction methods are probes in which X-ray photons are scattered, absorbed or emitted by matter.
groups.rank_note: n/a

groups.statement: Particle and radiation probes are non-X-ray interactions in which particles or long-wavelength radiation are used to examine matter.
groups.rank_note: n/a

groups.statement: Emission and impact phenomena are processes in which electrons, ions or heat are released from solids and liquids by thermal or collisional excitation.
groups.rank_note: n/a

groups.statement: Photon-driven impact phenomena are kinds of laser-matter interaction whose scale is set by the photon quantum ħω and the speed of light c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from general laser impact to ablation to multiphoton absorption.

groups.statement: Electron-impact emission phenomena are kinds of surface response to incident electrons, with scales set by ħ and the electron energy.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: Auger, secondary, other emission, then energy loss.

groups.statement: Desorption, positron and heavy-particle beam processes are kinds of particle ejection or surface interaction driven by stimulated or beam impact.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: stimulated desorption, positron emission, then ion and atom beams.

groups.statement: Photoemission from distinct material surfaces are kinds of photoelectron spectra differing in the sample type probed, with scales set by ħ and the photon energy.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: clean surfaces, liquids, adsorbed layers, polymers, disordered structures.

groups.statement: Low-dimensional and many-body framings are kinds of system descriptions in which the particle number N and nonequilibrium statistics set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: disordered and interface systems, then 2D systems, growth, and nonequilibrium statistics.

groups.statement: The classification headings frame the whole area of materials fabrication, treatment, testing and analysis.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the broadest heading to the specific-materials heading.

groups.statement: Metals, semimetals and alloys are conductive materials whose properties arise from metallic bonding.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the metallic class to its carbon-based relative.

groups.statement: Semiconductors are materials with intermediate conductivity, divided by their elemental, compound, organic or amorphous makeup.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from elemental through compound to organic, amorphous and other.

groups.statement: Bulk inorganic and organic solids include other semiconductors, ceramics, glasses and polymers, each defined by its bonding and network structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from other semiconductors to ceramics, glasses and polymers.

groups.statement: Composite, porous and engineered media combine several phases or structured components to obtain properties not found in a single homogeneous material.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from ceramic and metal composites to porous and engineered media.

groups.statement: Bulk and extended carbon allotropes are materials whose properties are set by a very large number N of covalently bonded carbon atoms in a lattice.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the carbon lattice.

groups.statement: Designed and molecular carbon-based materials are finite, engineered or molecule-sized structures whose scale is fixed by a small number of atoms.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the molecular unit.

groups.statement: Nanostructured bulk forms are aggregates of nanometre-sized grains or particles whose scale is set by the number of atoms in each grain.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the aggregate.

groups.statement: Low-dimensional nanostructures and devices are objects confined along one or more directions, where size and quantum effects governed by ħ set their behaviour.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of confinement dimensionality.

groups.statement: Quantum-confined semiconductor structures and crystal growth theory cover systems whose energy scale is set by ħ and by the number of atoms in the crystal.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of confinement and growth.

groups.statement: Vapor-phase growth methods build crystals or films by condensing or reacting species supplied from a gas or vapor source.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS listing from general vapor growth to specific vapor-deposition techniques.

groups.statement: Liquid-phase growth methods produce crystals or films from solutions, melts, or electrolytes in which the material is dissolved or molten.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from bulk crystal growth in liquids to liquid-based film deposition.

groups.statement: Solid-phase growth methods form crystals or epitaxial layers by transformation, diffusion, or recrystallization within an existing solid.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from bulk solid-state growth to solid-phase epitaxy.

groups.statement: Beam-assisted, spray, and theoretical approaches to film growth rely on directed energetic beams, sprayed material, or models of the growth process rather than on a bulk growth medium.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, following the PACS listing of the general film-growth category.

groups.statement: Pulsed laser ablation deposition and deposition by sputtering are physical vapor thin-film growth techniques in which material is ejected from a solid target onto a substrate.
Bulk mechanical and thermal shaping methods work macroscopic workpieces by forming, joining, cutting or consolidating them.
groups.rank_note: Coarsest scale: macroscopic bulk workpieces.

groups.statement: Bulk chemical and phase-based processing methods make or refine materials through reactions, precipitation, dispersal in aerosols, purification or solidification.
groups.rank_note: Bulk to mesoscale: materials made or refined chemically or by phase change.

groups.statement: Chemical and catalytic nanosynthesis methods build nanoscale structures by driving reactions in a controlled way.
groups.rank_note: Nanoscale structures built by chemical reaction.

groups.statement: Directed patterning and atomic-scale methods impose structure on a surface by writing, depositing or placing material at the finest scales.
groups.rank_note: Finest scale: patterns written and atoms placed individually.

groups.statement: Laser-assisted deposition and micro- and nanoscale pattern formation are further fabrication techniques whose claims are scaled by the governing constants c, ħ, G and N.
Phase diagrams are kinds of equilibrium maps that show which phases are stable in a given class of material.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code, from metals, alloys and oxides to other materials.

groups.statement: Phase transformations are kinds of structural change in which a material moves from one phase or arrangement to another.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code, from solidification through solid-solid and martensitic changes to precipitation.

groups.statement: Thermal and thermomechanical treatments are kinds of processing that use heat and working to alter a material's microstructure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code, from the general heading to hardening, cold working and other heat treatments.

groups.statement: Mechanical responses are kinds of material behavior under load, including elastic, plastic, failure and wear behavior.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code, from elasticity through plasticity and fracture to wear.

groups.statement: Property-changing and surface treatments are kinds of external processing that modify electrical, optical or surface characteristics of a material.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code, from property effects through pressure and radiation to surface treatments.

groups.statement: Surface treatments are processes that modify, protect or finish the surface of a material.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Property testing methods probe how a material responds to loads or to unusual environments such as microgravity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Nondestructive testing methods inspect a material's interior or surface without damaging it, using sound, electromagnetic fields, light or tomography.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Physical chemistry topics and system descriptors cover the dynamics of chemical processes and the kinds of systems in which they occur.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the classification scheme.

groups.statement: Gettering and surface hardening by nitridation or carburization are further materials-processing treatments whose scale is set not by c, ħ, G or N alone but by the diffusion and reaction of impurity atoms within a solid.
Statistical and classical rate theories treat reacting systems with thermal averages and trajectories, so N and thermal energy set their scale rather than ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from statistical theories to classical trajectory models.

groups.statement: Quantum and semiclassical treatments of reactions are those whose scale is set by Planck's constant ħ through tunneling, resonances and isotope mass effects.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from full quantum theory to semiclassical and quantum-effect topics.

groups.statement: Topics on potential energy surfaces, non-adiabatic crossings and state-resolved energy flow describe how electronic structure governs reaction dynamics and products.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from surfaces to non-adiabatic transitions to resulting energy transfer and products.

groups.statement: Quantitative and computational treatments of reactivity concern measured or simulated rate constants and the effect of the environment on them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from measured rate quantities to simulation to solvent environment.

groups.statement: Specific reaction classes are distinguished by the chemical species involved, such as radicals, ions or positronium, with electromagnetic and mass scales setting their behavior.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general mechanisms to neutral radical reactions to charged and exotic species.

groups.statement: Elementary reaction types are the basic ways in which molecules transform, by exchanging groups, breaking apart, combining, or rearranging.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the transformation: exchange, decomposition, association, isomerization.

groups.statement: Solvent and catalytic interactions are effects in solution that steer or speed reactions without being a reaction type themselves.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: hydrogen bonding, then homogeneous catalysis.

groups.statement: Confined or structured media are condensed or nanoscale hosts in which reactions occur on, within, or inside a defined structure.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of host: clusters, zeolites, porous media, micelles, solids.

groups.statement: Energetic or gas-phase environments are settings of extreme or dilute conditions where reactions proceed in fluids, flames, plasmas, the atmosphere, or vapor deposition.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of environment: supercritical, atmospheric, combustion, plasma, deposition.

groups.statement: Polymer chemistry covers the properties, reactions, and polymerization of macromolecules, including conducting polymers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general polymers to the conducting specialization.

groups.statement: Polymer materials studied through their optical response and their interactions with surfaces or embedded nanoscale fillers.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from optical response to surface adhesion to embedded nanoparticles.

groups.statement: Polymer classes defined by chemical composition or bulk physical behaviour, such as copolymers, polyelectrolytes, biopolymers and general polymer properties.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general properties to specific polymer classes.

groups.statement: Studies that probe or manipulate individual molecules to observe their kinetics, reactions and photochemistry one molecule at a time.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general single-molecule kinetics to specific manipulation techniques.

groups.statement: Chemical kinetics inside living systems, covering enzymes, charge transfer, nucleic acids, complex reactions and membrane transport.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general biological kinetics to specific processes.

groups.statement: General chemical kinetics in special regimes, including membrane and ion-exchange processes and nonlinear dynamics such as oscillations, chaos and bifurcations.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from membrane processes to general regimes to nonlinear dynamics.

groups.statement: Reaction-dynamics phenomena are kinds of chemical change in which spatial or temporal organization, shock loading or complexity governs how a reaction proceeds.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure, from pattern formation in bulk reactions to shock-driven and complex systems.

groups.statement: Electrochemical processes are kinds of chemical change driven by or producing electric current, such as synthesis, corrosion, electrolysis and deposition.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure, from synthesis and corrosion to electrolysis and electrodeposition.

groups.statement: Electrochemical cell components and interfaces are the physical parts where charge transfer occurs, including electrodes, electrolytes, films and reactive surfaces.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure, from electrodes and electrolytes to films and surfaces.

groups.statement: Electrochemical materials are classes of solid substance, such as dielectrics, semiconductors, polymers and ceramics, whose properties are used in electrochemical systems.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure across the material classes.

groups.statement: Electrochemical measurement and biological applications are uses of electrochemical methods for chemical analysis and for studying living systems.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure, analytical use first and biological use second.

groups.statement: General and engineering topics in electrochemistry cover nanostructured materials, applied electrochemistry and process engineering that are not tied to one specific device.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from broad materials and applications to engineering practice.

groups.statement: Electrochemical energy storage devices store charge or energy in batteries, supercapacitors or hybrid photoelectrochemical cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from batteries to capacitors and hybrid devices.

groups.statement: Fuel cells convert chemical fuel directly into electricity and are classed by their electrolyte type.
groups.rank_note: Ordered as in the classification, from solid-oxide to other fuel cells.

groups.statement: Photochemistry topics describe chemical processes driven by radiation, divided by the kind of radiation or by how the reaction is controlled.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from photochemistry in general, then by radiation type from infrared to X-rays, then control and multiphoton processes.

groups.statement: Photochemistry concepts form a kinds group in which controlling photochemical reactions is a specialized case of general photochemistry, where light-driven molecular processes are set by the photon energy ħω (ħ and c) acting on collections of N molecules.
Femtosecond pump-probe and coherent techniques follow the dynamics of isolated atoms and molecules, such as dissociation and bound-state motion, on ultrafast timescales.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general field to specific experiment types.

groups.statement: Femtosecond probes are applied to molecules and nanostructures in different media, such as semiconductors, biological systems, surfaces, liquids and solids.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by the type of host environment probed.

groups.statement: NMR methods are the general resonance technique and its high-resolution, multidimensional and pulse-sequence forms, whose scale is set by Planck's constant and nuclear magnetic moments.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general technique to specific methods.

groups.statement: NMR studies of nuclear species, molecular motion and spin relaxation describe how nuclear spins behave and exchange energy in a sample.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from nuclear species to motion to relaxation.

groups.statement: Structure determination of biomolecules by NMR and the thermodynamics of reactions are characterization topics whose scale is set by the number of particles and bulk energy changes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from structural characterization to thermodynamic characterization.

groups.statement: Thermodynamics of chemical systems covers the energetic and equilibrium properties of substances, solutions, nuclei and small particles.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Disperse systems are mixtures in which one phase is spread through another, such as colloids, gels, emulsions and aerosols.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Self-assembled molecular structures are ordered assemblies formed by amphiphilic molecules or by synthesized and modeled framework structures.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Zeolite and molecular-sieve studies concern how molecules, clusters and reactions behave inside porous crystalline solids.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Chemical analysis methods are physical techniques used to identify and measure the composition of a sample.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS code sequence.

groups.statement: Mass spectrometry methods identify substances by measuring the mass-to-charge ratio of ions they produce.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general technique to its specific variants.

groups.statement: Spectroscopic methods analyze a sample by how it absorbs, emits, or converts photons, electrons, and other radiation.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by the type of radiation or energy exchange probed.

groups.statement: Analytical methods that identify or measure a sample's composition through electrochemical response, induced radioactivity, ion backscattering, or electromagnetic probing, rather than through spectra or ion masses.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by the physical mechanism of the method.

groups.statement: The rheology framework covers the field heading and the basic description of deformation and flow.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the field heading to its basic descriptions.

groups.statement: Rheology theories and models are the theoretical and simulation frameworks used to relate stress, deformation, and molecular motion.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from continuum descriptions to molecular-scale models.

groups.statement: Particle-level dynamics and simulation methods treat a fluid through its many interacting particles, so the particle number N sets the scale of the claim.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from particle dynamics to simulation to structural change; N is the governing constant.

groups.statement: Basic deformation and flow geometries describe how a material is sheared, stretched or driven through a channel, with scale set by classical continuum quantities.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general deformation to specific flow geometries; none of c, hbar, G or N governs.

groups.statement: Wall slip and boundary effects concern how a flowing material moves relative to its confining surface, a classical interfacial scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general slip effects to apparent slip; no fundamental constants govern.

groups.statement: Material processing and mixing applications cover industrial operations that shape or blend flowing materials, at classical engineering scales.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from forming operations to blending; no fundamental constants govern.

groups.statement: Material behavior topics describe the stress response of complex fluids, whether elastic, viscous, yielding or time-dependent, at the classical continuum scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the general category through viscoelastic, flow-rate-dependent, and time-dependent responses; no fundamental constants govern.

groups.statement: Flow and deformation phenomena are rheological behaviors that appear when a material is sheared, heated, stressed or driven unstable.
groups.rank_note: Phenomena are listed by structure in PACS numbering order, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Solid and structured materials are rigid or network-forming media, such as glasses, granular solids, gels and field-responsive fluids, whose rheology is set by their internal structure.
groups.rank_note: Members are listed by structure in PACS numbering order, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Dispersed and reacting soft-matter systems are multiphase or chemically evolving materials, such as suspensions, emulsions, foams and micellar solutions, in which a dispersed phase or reaction controls flow.
groups.rank_note: Members are listed by structure in PACS numbering order, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Natural and biological materials are naturally occurring media, such as blood, collagen, wood, rock and ice, whose rheology is studied as found in nature.
groups.rank_note: Members are listed by structure in PACS numbering order, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Polymer fluids are flowing materials built from long-chain molecules, whether dissolved in a solvent, molten or mixed with other polymers.
groups.rank_note: Members are listed by structure in PACS numbering order, not ranked by degree.

groups.statement: Polymer materials are soft solids built from long-chain macromolecules, whose mechanics is set by chain number density N and thermal energy.
groups.rank_note: structure

groups.statement: Mechanical rheological tests probe how a material deforms and flows under imposed stress or strain, ranked from the general technique to specific tests.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the general technique (rheometry) to specific tests of viscosity, normal stress, extension, relaxation, creep and oscillation.

groups.statement: Optical, magnetic resonance and scattering probes and data analysis reveal the microscopic structure of flowing materials.
groups.rank_note: structure

groups.statement: Electronics topics cover circuits and their theory, which is governed by classical electromagnetism rather than the constants of rheology.
groups.rank_note: structure

groups.statement: Time-domain and frequency-domain rheometric tests that probe a material's viscoelastic response by applying a small controlled shear stress or strain and measuring the resulting deformation.
Power electronics and amplifiers are active circuits that supply, condition, or boost electrical power and signal strength.
groups.rank_note: First in structural order: active power-handling circuits that feed the rest.

groups.statement: Signal-generating and signal-shaping circuits create or transform waveforms by oscillating, modulating, pulsing, or digitally switching signals.
groups.rank_note: Second: active signal-processing circuits built on the power stage.

groups.statement: Passive circuit components are devices that connect, resist, store, or protect without providing gain, such as switches, resistors, inductors, capacitors, and fuses.
groups.rank_note: Third: passive elements that make up the basic circuit building blocks.

groups.statement: Filters and radiowave guiding structures select frequencies and carry or radiate electromagnetic signals along lines, guides, and antennas.
groups.rank_note: Fourth: frequency-selective and signal-carrying structures linking circuits to waves.

groups.statement: Microwave devices and communication systems generate, process, and transmit high-frequency signals using tubes, masers, integrated circuits, and satellite links.
groups.rank_note: Last: high-frequency devices and system-level telecommunications.

groups.statement: Remote sensing and general conversion performance topics are scaled mainly by the speed of light c and by bulk figures of merit, with no quantum coherence required.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the most classical, c-scaled signalling and bulk metrics, which sit lowest in quantum content.

groups.statement: Thermal, plasma and photon-driven direct converters set their scale by ħ through band gaps and work functions, together with the large particle number N of the working medium.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from weakly quantum, N-dominated thermal and plasma conversion to photoelectric conversion, where ħ sets the photon energy.

groups.statement: Energy storage and high-power superconducting hardware rely on macroscopic coherent states whose scale is set by ħ and N but is used only at the bulk, classical-engineering level.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from conventional capacitor storage to superconducting magnets, cables and wires, which use macroscopic quantum coherence more.

groups.statement: General superconducting electronic devices and Josephson and SQUID elements have their scale fixed by the flux quantum h/2e, so ħ sets the measured quantity directly.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from broad device categories and modeling to Josephson and SQUID devices, where ħ is most direct.

groups.statement: Superconducting logic, memory and detector devices operate near quantum limits, with ħ setting the gap energy and single-photon sensitivity.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from logic and memory circuits to single-photon detectors that are the most quantum-limited.

groups.statement: Macroscopic quantum coherence devices operate on phase coherence whose scale is set by the flux quantum h/2e, so ħ governs them.
groups.rank_note: Kinds distinguished by the phase-coherent quantum constant ħ.

groups.statement: Quantum confinement and tunneling devices have behavior whose scale is set by ħ through electron confinement and barrier tunneling.
groups.rank_note: Kinds distinguished by confinement and tunneling governed by ħ.

groups.statement: Semiconductor devices are governed by the collective behavior of very large numbers N of carriers rather than individual quanta.
groups.rank_note: Kinds distinguished by many-carrier junction and bulk transport.

groups.statement: Integrated-circuit fabrication topics have a scale set by the very large number N of devices and features integrated together.
groups.rank_note: Kinds distinguished by integration of enormous numbers of components.

groups.statement: Thyristors, bipolar transistors, and junction diodes are semiconductor junction devices whose behavior is governed by the charge carrier physics of p-n junctions, where Planck's constant ħ sets the quantum scale of the band structure and the number of carriers N sets the scale of the current.
Classical processing and magnetic device topics are scaled mainly by the particle number N, with no essential role for c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Fewest constants: N alone sets the scale.

groups.statement: Vacuum electron emission topics are scaled by ħ through quantum tunnelling together with N, the number of emitting sites.
groups.rank_note: Two constants: ħ and N.

groups.statement: Dielectric and magnetic-response device topics are scaled by ħ-based collective quantum polarization and magnetization together with N.
groups.rank_note: Two constants: ħ and N, with collective response.

groups.statement: Photon detection topics are scaled by ħ and c through single-photon absorption and by N through the number of carriers.
groups.rank_note: Three constants: c, ħ and N.

groups.statement: Light emission and display topics are scaled by c, ħ and N through photon energy, light propagation and the number of emitters.
groups.rank_note: Most constants: c, ħ and N jointly.

groups.statement: Magnetic recording, head, levitation, and magnetooptical devices rely on classical magnetization, with scales set mainly by c in the optical case and by macroscopic fields otherwise.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from thin-film heads through storage media and levitation to magnetooptics.

groups.statement: Spintronic memory devices store bits through spin-polarized transport, with scales set by ħ through spin and tunneling physics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general spintronics heading to specific memory types.

groups.statement: Spin-polarized transistor, tunnel-junction, Hall, and sensor devices control or detect carriers through quantum spin-dependent transport, with scales set by ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from transistors and tunnel junctions to Hall devices and sensors.

groups.statement: Thermoelectromagnetic devices convert between heat, electricity, and magnetism, with scales set by macroscopic transport coefficients rather than by individual quantum constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general heading to thermoelectric, magnetoelectric, and magnetothermal devices.

groups.statement: General theoretical frameworks for small or random systems have scales set by particle number N and fluctuations rather than by c, ħ, or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from small systems through stochastic processes to general biological theory.

groups.statement: Continuum and analytical modeling methods describe biological matter through smooth fields and equations, so their scale is set by macroscopic material constants rather than by ħ or N explicitly.
groups.rank_note: Continuum methods, ordered from analytical theory to numerical solution.

groups.statement: Statistical and particle-based simulation methods treat biological systems as ensembles of many discrete units, so the particle number N and thermal fluctuations set their scale.
groups.rank_note: Methods ordered from lattice and stochastic models to sampling and dynamics simulations.

groups.statement: Information-bearing and structural macromolecules are built from long chains whose coding and folding depend on quantum-chemical bonding scales set by ħ and on large monomer number N.
groups.rank_note: Polymer classes ordered from information-level description to chain types.

groups.statement: Functional protein assemblies are specialized protein forms whose activity or architecture arises from molecular-scale chemistry set by ħ and by cooperative assembly of many units N.
groups.rank_note: Protein-based classes ordered from catalytic to structural to membrane-bound forms.

groups.statement: Small signaling and metabolic biomolecules are low-mass compounds whose behavior is set by molecular quantum chemistry through ħ with few units N involved.
groups.rank_note: Small-molecule classes ordered from structural lipids and sugars to regulatory hormones and vitamins.

groups.statement: Claims about electronic, spectral and bonding properties of biomolecules are set directly by ħ through quantum energy levels and bond energies.
groups.rank_note: Most ħ-dependent: scale fixed by quantum electronic structure.

groups.statement: Claims about the molecular identity and structure of the nucleic-acid building blocks are set by quantum chemistry through ħ and the electron charge and mass.
groups.rank_note: Second: chemical structure rooted in quantum chemistry with ħ setting atomic and bond sizes.

groups.statement: Claims about molecular interactions, mechanics and reaction rates combine ħ-derived interaction strengths with thermal energy, so both ħ and N-scale thermal factors matter.
groups.rank_note: Middle: mixed dependence on interaction energies from ħ and thermal energy.

groups.statement: Claims about transport and noise in solution are set by thermal motion of many molecules, so N and the thermal energy scale dominate over ħ.
groups.rank_note: Fourth: ħ enters only indirectly through fixed material parameters.

groups.statement: Claims about folding, sequence statistics and coarse-grained models are set by the large number N of degrees of freedom and by combinatorics, largely independent of ħ, c and G.
groups.rank_note: Least ħ-dependent: scale set by N and statistical mechanics.

groups.statement: Computational and theoretical methods are approaches whose scale is set by the many-particle number N and by ħ where quantum effects enter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from analytical to numerical methods.

groups.statement: Structural organization classes describe how many atoms are arranged into molecular and aggregate architectures, so scale is set by N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from local to global organization.

groups.statement: Dynamical processes are time-dependent motions of molecules whose scale is set by the number of interacting particles N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from interactions to large-scale motion.

groups.statement: Binding interactions are couplings between a protein and a partner such as a polynucleotide, protein, ligand, solvent or membrane, with scale set by N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, by type of binding partner.

groups.statement: Light-driven quantum events are fast electronic and photon-induced processes whose scale is set by ħ and c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from ultrafast transfer to bond breaking and ionization.

groups.statement: Photon-linked molecular processes are those where the quantum constant ħ and the speed of light c set the energy scale of light emission.
groups.rank_note: Single-member-type grouping ordered by structure; light emission governed by ħ and c.

groups.statement: Phase-change and assembly processes are those where the number of molecules N and thermal energy set the scale of collective ordering or breakup of matter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from dissolving and aggregating to ordered crystals and chains.

groups.statement: Modeling and membrane-boundary topics are those where the scale is set by the elasticity and thermal fluctuations of many lipid molecules N rather than by c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general theory to bounding envelopes.

groups.statement: Filament and motor-driven mechanical systems are those where the scale is set by piconewton forces and thermal energy acting on N protein units rather than by c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from static filaments to motile appendages.

groups.statement: Organelle and transport systems are those where the scale is set by the ion and cargo counts N and electrochemical energies, with ħ entering only through molecular binding.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from stored genome and organelles to transport and channels.

groups.statement: Network and signaling claims describe how many interacting molecules form regulatory circuits and transmit signals, with N setting the scale.
groups.rank_note: Molecular-circuit level of cell organization.

groups.statement: Method claims are theoretical and computational tools, such as analytical theory, Monte Carlo, lattice models and simulation, that treat large-N cell systems statistically.
groups.rank_note: Methodological level of description.

groups.statement: Physical-property claims describe the measurable physics of membranes and nuclei, including fluctuations, mechanics, transport and structure, as large-N continuum behavior.
groups.rank_note: Physical-property level of cell components.

groups.statement: Cell-process claims describe whole-cell activities such as growth, motion, shape formation and adhesion, whose scale is set by large molecule numbers N.
groups.rank_note: Whole-cell process level.

groups.statement: Nuclear morphology and membrane transport are cell-biophysics topics whose claims are scaled by which of the constants c, ħ, G and N set their governing scale.
Collective cell phenomena are those in which large numbers N of cells aggregate, communicate and self-organize into populations, biofilms and patterns.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from simple aggregation to communication to full pattern formation.

groups.statement: Molecular and network-level topics concern how many interacting genes, proteins and signaling components process information and fluctuate within cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from signaling networks to noise to omics-scale descriptions.

groups.statement: Whole-organism integrative topics describe large-scale biological processes and rhythms that emerge from the coordination of enormous numbers of cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from integrative processes to rhythms to organism-level properties.

groups.statement: Neural and excitable-tissue topics cover systems of many coupled excitable units whose collective electrical and mechanical activity is set by their number N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from synaptic networks to neuroscience to muscle and heart to tissue properties.

groups.statement: Transport and thermal physiology topics treat bulk flow of blood, air and heat through organisms as continuum processes of many molecules.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from thermal processes to blood flow to respiratory flow.

groups.statement: Cellular electrical signaling topics describe how charge, ion currents and fields carry signals along and between neurons.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from single axon to synapse and field effects.

groups.statement: Measurement and imaging techniques probe neural activity and anatomy using electromagnetic fields, magnetic resonance or light.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from electromagnetic recording to magnetic resonance to optical methods.

groups.statement: Collective dynamics topics treat the coordinated behavior of many interacting neurons as emergent network phenomena.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from network dynamics to synchronization, oscillation and pattern formation, with models spanning all.

groups.statement: Information and control topics treat neural activity as signals that are quantified, encoded, transformed and regulated.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from information measures to encoding to feedback control.

groups.statement: System-level and clinical topics concern the supporting cells, disease states and sensory and motor functions of the nervous system as a whole.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from supporting cells and disease to sensory input and motor output.

groups.statement: Adaptive and developmental processes are the ways living systems change, learn, grow and spend energy over time.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from neural adaptation to growth and energy use.

groups.statement: Material and structural properties describe the physical makeup of tissue, including its stiffness, electrical response, flow behavior and architecture.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from mechanical to electrical to fluid properties and overall structure.

groups.statement: Active motion and signaling phenomena are the ways tissues and organisms contract, transmit impulses and move through their environment.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from cellular contraction and signaling to whole-body movement.

groups.statement: Circulatory and barrier dynamics cover the transport of blood and the regulation of passage between body compartments.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from central organs to peripheral vessels to the brain barrier.

groups.statement: Infectious diseases are disorders caused by pathogenic agents such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, fungi and prions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally by pathogen type from bacteria to prions.

groups.statement: Disease groups rooted in molecular and genetic defects arise where the quantum-chemical scale set by ħ governs the underlying mechanism.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by how strongly a molecular, ħ-scale mechanism sets the disease origin, with the most strongly genetic first.

groups.statement: Neurological disorders are diseases of excitable tissue whose scale is set by electrochemical signaling among large numbers N of neurons.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from network-wide dysfunction to progressive neural degeneration.

groups.statement: Organ-system disorders of body structure and metabolism are set by macroscopic tissue mechanics and chemistry rather than by fundamental constants directly.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from mechanical load-bearing tissue to chemically regulated organ systems.

groups.statement: Collective dynamics of many interacting organisms are governed by the large number N of agents, not by microscopic constants.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from ecological systems at large to evolving populations and human social systems.

groups.statement: Effects of electromagnetic fields on living matter are set by photon energy ħω and the speed of light c, varying across the spectrum.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by increasing frequency, from static and low-frequency fields to optical and infrared radiation.

groups.statement: Acoustic and ultrasonic effects are mechanical wave interactions whose scale is set by classical continuum properties rather than by ħ.
groups.rank_note: Lowest in quantum energy: classical mechanical waves with no ħ scale.

groups.statement: Dosimetry, mechanism and therapy entries for the first electromagnetic exposure category of the 87.50 subsections, where classical field strengths govern the scale.
groups.rank_note: Low quantum energy: classical electromagnetic fields.

groups.statement: Entries for the second electromagnetic exposure category, covering mechanisms, dosimetry and therapy for field interactions that remain well below ionizing photon energies.
groups.rank_note: Intermediate quantum energy: field interactions still below the ionization threshold.

groups.statement: Entries for the third non-ionizing exposure category, covering mechanisms, dosimetry and therapy for radiation whose photon energy is set by ħ times frequency but stays below ionization.
groups.rank_note: Higher quantum energy: optical and radio-frequency photons below the ionization threshold.

groups.statement: Ionizing radiation effects and the remaining exposure entries involve photon energies high enough to ionize matter, so ħ and c set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Highest quantum energy: ionizing radiation.

groups.statement: Treatment delivery techniques are the specific therapeutic modalities by which radiation is applied to a patient.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general therapeutic applications to specific delivery techniques.

groups.statement: Treatment planning and strategy topics cover how a radiation treatment is designed and optimized before delivery.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from overall strategy to detailed design.

groups.statement: Computational methods are the simulation and algorithmic tools used to model radiation dose and its application.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from general simulation to specific algorithms and applications.

groups.statement: Safety and verification topics are the checks that confirm a radiation treatment is delivered correctly and safely.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from monitoring to quality assurance to verification records.

groups.statement: Dose and response assessment topics measure delivered dose and evaluate how tissue responds to it.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from dosimetry to tissue response to dose-volume analysis.

groups.statement: Radiation sources are the devices that generate the therapeutic beam, either by accelerating particles or by radioactive decay.
groups.rank_note: Parent category listed first, then its two kinds of source.

groups.statement: Collimation defines the size and shape of the radiation field using collimating devices.
groups.rank_note: Collimation as the whole, followed by its aspects: field size, field shaping and collimators.

groups.statement: Beam modification and support equipment covers the therapy devices that alter beam intensity or ensure its safe and accurate delivery.
groups.rank_note: General equipment heading first, then the specific kinds of support and modifying equipment.

groups.statement: Imaging modalities are the distinct techniques by which medical images of the body are formed.
groups.rank_note: General medical imaging heading first, then the specific modalities.

groups.statement: Image evaluation and analysis covers the measures of image quality and the computational tools used to interpret images.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from the broad quality measure to its specific resolution metric, then to analysis and diagnosis tools.

groups.statement: Image-quality limits are the properties of a recorded image whose scale is set by photon counting statistics N and by how radiation interacts with tissue.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from signal difference to unwanted variation and error.

groups.statement: Image processing operations are computational steps applied to recorded data, which depend on N only through the noise they must handle and not on c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from building the image to aligning, partitioning, smoothing and sharpening it.

groups.statement: CT scanner configurations are detector arrangements for x-ray tomography, in which the number of detected photons N sets the noise scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from one detector row to many rows.

groups.statement: Nuclear medicine methods detect gamma photons from administered radionuclides, so the photon energy ħω and the count N set their scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from planar imaging to tomographic imaging and the supporting agents and dose.

groups.statement: Projection x-ray techniques form images from transmitted x-ray photons, whose energy ħω and count N set the scale of contrast and noise.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the general method to static and dynamic projection imaging.

groups.statement: X-ray based imaging forms images from the attenuation of ionizing photons, so photon energy and quantum counting statistics set its scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: general X-ray detectors first, then mammography variants, then densitometry.

groups.statement: Magnetic resonance imaging is a single technique whose parts are the nuclear spin physics, hardware, acquisition protocols, and applications that set its scale through the Planck constant and the Larmor frequency.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from theory to instrumentation, then sequences, then imaging uses.

groups.statement: Methods that probe tissue with non-ionizing waves or currents are scaled by propagation speed and tissue conductivity rather than photon energy.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by depth of tissue penetration, from the deepest (ultrasonography) to electrical methods.

groups.statement: Clinical applications, pulse sequences, and instrumentation are the practical facets of magnetic resonance imaging, each defined by the physical constants that set the scale of its signal and resolution.
Bone densitometry and computed radiography are X-ray imaging techniques whose scale is set by the photon-matter interaction, which depends on ħ and c rather than on gravity.
Classical wave and image-processing methods are scaled by wave speed and signal handling rather than by quantum constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from acoustic imaging to image processing and simulation.

groups.statement: Optical probes of tissue are scaled by the speed of light and the photon energy set by ħ, with c and ħ together fixing the wavelength and energy.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from broad light transmission to specific scattering and microscopy methods.

groups.statement: Particle-wave diffraction and microscopy methods are scaled by the de Broglie wavelength, which depends on ħ.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from diffraction to microscopy and simulation.

groups.statement: Spin-resonance spectroscopies are scaled by ħ together with the magnetic moment of the spins being probed.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from electron to nuclear spin resonance.

groups.statement: Spectroscopies of quantized molecular and core-level transitions are scaled by ħ and the discrete energy levels of the sample.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general spectroscopy to infrared and x-ray methods.

groups.statement: Spectroscopic probes of quantized energy levels in matter are scaled by ħ, with c entering through the photon energy and electron or nuclear transitions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the governing constants.

groups.statement: Classical far-field light microscopy contrast modes have a resolution scale set by wavelength, that is by c and ħ through the photon, without quantum nonlinearity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the governing constants.

groups.statement: Advanced optical imaging methods exploit quantum optical processes or evanescent fields to go beyond the ordinary diffraction scale set by ħ and c.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the governing constants.

groups.statement: Force-based manipulation methods are scaled by photon momentum (ħ and c) or by mechanical forces acting on single molecules and cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the governing constants.

groups.statement: Electrical, magnetic resonance and separation methods are scaled by ensemble statistics (N) and charge or spin properties of many particles.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the governing constants.

groups.statement: Molecular profiling techniques are kinds of methods that read out biological molecules such as genes and proteins.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 87.80 classification.

groups.statement: Neural and prosthetic fields are kinds of engineering that interface with the nervous system or replace body functions.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 87.85 classification.

groups.statement: Tissue and mechanics fields are kinds of engineering that deal with the physical and material behavior of living tissue.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 87.85 classification.

groups.statement: Sensing and modeling fields are kinds of engineering that acquire, process, image or simulate biomedical signals and systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 87.85 classification.

groups.statement: Small-scale fabrication and manipulation fields are kinds of engineering that build or handle devices at micro and nano scales.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS 87.85 classification.

groups.statement: Neural interfacing and modeling topics concern devices and models that connect with or describe the nervous system and cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from models to devices; not a ranking by constants.
