groups.statement: Stimulation safety topics concern electrode stimulation of tissue and the limits that prevent harm to it.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from stimulation to its limits and damage; not a ranking by constants.

groups.statement: Control and sensing topics concern signal flow, feedback loops, and sensors used to monitor and communicate with biological systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from control schemes to sensing and communication; not a ranking by constants.

groups.statement: Materials and mechanics topics concern the physical properties, motion, and compatibility of biological and bio-based matter.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from mechanics to materials and compatibility; not a ranking by constants.

groups.statement: Integrative and genetic biology topics concern whole-system regulation and the engineering or study of genes and genomes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered structurally from systems-level to genetic topics; not a ranking by constants.

groups.statement: Broad top-level headings frame the whole field of energy and related resource topics at the largest scale.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Physical and energy-content analyses set the quantitative limits and standards of energy production and use.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Policy and economic issues concern the targets, assessment, costs and trading mechanisms that govern energy at the societal scale.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Environmental and conservation aspects deal with reducing the impact and demand of energy use in agriculture and equipment.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Sector-specific energy uses cover heating, lighting, industry and transportation at the scale of individual applications.
groups.rank_note: ordered by structure

groups.statement: Heat-source resources are the natural underground sources of heat and fluid that geothermal energy is drawn from.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from dry hot rock to fluid-bearing reservoirs and their surface or well outputs.

groups.statement: Reservoir engineering covers the methods and equipment used to create, access and isolate productive geothermal reservoirs.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from reservoir stimulation to pumping and zonal isolation.

groups.statement: Characterization and modelling covers the tools and models used to image, measure and predict the behaviour of geothermal rock and fluid.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from numerical models to imaging, downhole sensing and fracture characterization.

groups.statement: Power plants are the facilities that convert geothermal heat into electricity, whether by direct steam or flashed fluid.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from the general topic of electricity production to the two plant types.

groups.statement: Heat use and flux covers how geothermal heat flows through the Earth and is used directly for heating and cooling.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from direct-use applications to global, continental and oceanic heat flux.

groups.statement: Biomass source materials are the plant, residue and aquatic raw materials from which biomass energy is obtained.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from woody and crop sources to residues and aquatic sources.

groups.statement: Biomass general and source-level categories name the overall biomass energy field and its energy sources.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the whole field to its sources.

groups.statement: Biomass processing and fuel production topics cover the steps that turn biomass feedstock into usable fuel.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from fuel type to processing routes and conversion methods.

groups.statement: Biomass end uses and societal topics cover the products, power systems, markets and social issues that follow from biomass energy.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from products and power systems to markets and social issues.

groups.statement: Geothermal plants and extraction industries are non-biomass energy and resource topics based on heat or on removing materials from the ground.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from the steam plant to mineral and metals extraction.

groups.statement: Waste and decaying organic materials serve as raw feedstocks from which bioenergy is obtained.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from food waste to municipal waste to landfill and decaying matter.

groups.statement: Alcohol fuels are liquid biofuels in which the fuel molecule is an alcohol.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from ethanol to methanol to butanol to mixed alcohols.

groups.statement: Oil-derived and drop-in liquid fuels are made from oils or synthesized into hydrocarbon or ether fuels.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from biodiesel and vegetable oils to ethers, aviation fuel and F-T liquids.

groups.statement: Gaseous and solid fuels are non-liquid energy carriers produced from biomass.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from hydrogen and methane to syngas and pelletized solid fuel.

groups.statement: Conversion routes are the processes by which biomass is turned into usable fuel.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure, from Fischer-Tropsch synthesis to digestion to biochemical and thermochemical routes.

groups.statement: Biomass conversion pathways are the chemical and biological processes that turn raw biomass into fuels or intermediates.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure of process type; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Thermal power systems are installations that burn or thermally decompose biomass to generate energy or fuel gases and liquids.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure of system type; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Bio-based materials and industries are the products and sectors that use biomass as a raw material for manufactured goods.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure of product type; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Biomass energy end uses are the forms in which biomass-derived energy and products are finally delivered and consumed.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure of end-use type; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Broader context topics are the policy debate and the alternative hydrogen technology that frame biomass fuel use.
groups.rank_note: Listed by structure of topic type; no ranking implied.

groups.statement: Hydrogen production routes are the distinct processes by which hydrogen is generated, whether thermochemically, electrolytically, photolytically, or from biomass and the water-gas-shift reaction.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by production process.

groups.statement: Fuel cell system topics cover the overall plant around the cell, including its design and the supporting subsystems for fuel processing, power conversion and heat recovery.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from overall design to subsystems.

groups.statement: Fuel cell components are the physical building blocks of a cell assembly, centred on the stack.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from component heading to the stack.

groups.statement: Fuel cell materials and protection concern the substances used to build cell components and the means of protecting them against corrosion.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from general materials to specific material classes.

groups.statement: Water-gas-shift and biomass reforming are hydrogen-production processes governed by chemical kinetics and thermodynamics, so no fundamental constant among c, ħ, G or N sets their scale.
Electrolyte-based fuel cells are cell types defined by the electrolyte that carries ions between the electrodes.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: each member is a distinct electrolyte type.

groups.statement: Fuel-fed and regenerative cell variants are fuel cell kinds defined by how their fuel is supplied or recycled.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: each member is a distinct fuel or recycling arrangement.

groups.statement: Hydrogen storage materials are alternative solid media that hold hydrogen for use in fuel cells.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: each member is a distinct storage material.

groups.statement: Solar energy collection and conversion covers the parts of the chain that gathers sunlight and turns it into electricity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from the resource through concentrators to cells.

groups.statement: Solar cell development and application covers the parts of designing, testing and deploying photovoltaic systems.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure: from modeling and materials to testing and building use.

groups.statement: Concentrating solar thermal systems use mirrors or collectors to focus sunlight onto a receiver to generate heat or power.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from dish and tower systems to the collectors that supply them.

groups.statement: Photovoltaic cell types are the distinct semiconductor and material technologies used to convert sunlight directly into electricity.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from silicon to thin films, multijunction and organic cells.

groups.statement: Solar heating and cooling systems use sunlight to supply thermal energy for space, water, or pool temperature control.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from general systems to active, passive, and pool heating.

groups.statement: Solar electric and lighting applications are installations that put photovoltaic power or daylight to use in grids, buildings, and outdoor settings.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from grid-tied systems to building-integrated forms and outdoor lights.

groups.statement: Building-integrated solar applications are ways of using sunlight directly in the structure of a building, such as through natural daylighting and through roof top shingles.
The wind energy chain runs from the wind resource through turbine conversion and grid generation to the social issues that result.
groups.rank_note: Ordered from resource to conversion to generation to social effects.

groups.statement: Wind turbine research and development is made up of modeling and design, components, and testing activities.
groups.rank_note: Parts of the research and development effort.

groups.statement: Wind farms come in kinds distinguished by their scale and siting, from small-scale to large-scale and off-shore installations.
groups.rank_note: Ranked by scale and siting, from the general category to small, large and off-shore farms.

groups.statement: Hydropower technology divides into the general field, conventional hydropower, hydroturbines and emerging technologies.
groups.rank_note: Kinds of hydropower subject areas.

groups.statement: Hydropower installations include kinds of facilities and machinery such as dams, diversion works, pumped storage and cross-flow turbines.
groups.rank_note: Kinds of hydropower facilities and equipment.

groups.statement: Reaction and flow-driven turbines extract energy from water passing over or through the runner blades.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of runner type.

groups.statement: Impulse-type hydropower uses the direct kinetic energy of falling or flowing water, as in jets striking buckets or natural river flow.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the water-driven mechanism.

groups.statement: Ocean energy sources draw on the motion or the heat of the sea, from waves and tides to currents and thermal gradients.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of ocean resource.

groups.statement: Energy delivery covers the infrastructure that carries and distributes power from generators to users.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of delivery layer.

groups.statement: Energy storage technologies hold energy for later use in chemical, electrostatic or magnetic form.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of storage mechanism.

groups.statement: Wired transmission systems carry electrical power through conductors in grids, whether as ac, high-voltage dc, or superconducting lines.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the conductor system

groups.statement: Wireless power transmission sends electrical energy across space without conductors, for example by radio-frequency beams.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the transmission mechanism

groups.statement: Advanced vehicle types are distinguished by the kind of propulsion energy source they use, such as fuel cells, plug-in hybrids, or batteries.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the propulsion system

groups.statement: Vehicle energy storage devices store electrical energy on board, as lead-acid or nickel-metal hydride batteries or as ultracapacitors.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the storage technology

groups.statement: Alternative vehicle fuels and their fueling stations are the chemical fuels, such as biodiesel, propane, natural gas, and hydrogen, that replace conventional fuel, together with the stations that supply them.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the fuel supply chain

groups.statement: Biofuel-related entries are ethanol and fuel blends used as renewable alternative fuels.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing, ethanol first then blends.

groups.statement: Fossil fuel entries are the carbon-based energy resources of coal, oil and natural gas, together with the general fossil fuels heading.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing, general heading first then specific fuels.

groups.statement: Nuclear power entries are the energy sources that draw on fission or fusion of atomic nuclei.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing, fission then fusion.

groups.statement: Technology and application entries are the interdisciplinary uses of physics in industry, defense, computing, the web, engineering and forensics.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure of the PACS listing, from the general heading to specific applications.

groups.statement: This group collects further applications of physics to technology and society, such as the Internet, military systems and arms control, and other interdisciplinary uses, where no fundamental constant such as c, ħ, G or N sets the scale of the claim.
Air transportation and environmental topics form a set of applied human-infrastructure and environment concerns in which no fundamental constant sets the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Social and economic systems cover human populations, organizations, markets and cities, whose scale is set by the number of people or agents N.
groups.rank_note: Parent heading first, then its subtopics.

groups.statement: Information theory concerns quantifying information and its reliable transmission, with scale set by counts of bits and symbols rather than c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Parent heading first, then its subtopics.

groups.statement: Complexity measures count the computational and communication resources a problem requires, which scale with input size N.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by PACS numbering.

groups.statement: Complex systems are collections of many interacting parts whose collective scaling, structure, networks and patterns are governed by large N.
groups.rank_note: Parent heading first, then its subtopics.

groups.statement: Lattice and quantum model frameworks describe many-body systems on discrete sites, where ħ and the particle number N set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from statistical to quantum to condensed-matter lattice models.

groups.statement: Disorder-averaging and field-theoretic techniques are analytical methods whose scale is set by the number of degrees of freedom N rather than by c or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from replica and cavity methods to field theory.

groups.statement: Fractal characterizations quantify scale-invariant geometry, a purely geometric property that does not depend on c, ħ or G.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from dimension concepts to analysis methods.

groups.statement: Nonequilibrium growth and thermodynamic processes are classical phenomena governed by irreversibility and large N, not by quantum or relativistic constants.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from growth to irreversible processes to engines.

groups.statement: Materials-oriented topics concern the electronic, mechanical and nanoscale properties of real matter, where ħ and N set the scale.
groups.rank_note: Ordered by structure from the broad field to specific material properties.

groups.statement: Mechanical testing, robotics, packing and jamming, and minerals concern classical macroscopic systems whose scale is set by none of c, hbar, G or N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from fewest governing constants to most; this group has none, so it comes first.

groups.statement: Optimization problems, neural network simulations, numerical approximation, and series expansions are mathematical and computational methods whose claims carry no physical constant of their own.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from fewest governing constants to most; purely mathematical methods with no constants come after classical mechanics only by convention and precede N-dependent statistics.

groups.statement: Finite-size scaling and linear response theory are statistical tools whose claims are set by the particle number N, with hbar entering only when the response is quantum.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from fewest governing constants to most; N is the main scale here, with hbar optional.

groups.statement: Magnetism, methods in magnetism, superconductivity, and topological phases of matter are condensed-matter phenomena whose scale is set by hbar together with many-particle N.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from fewest governing constants to most; hbar and N together place this group fourth.

groups.statement: Quantum many-body systems, path-integral methods, quasiparticles, the Lindblad equation, interferometry, and gamma-ray techniques are quantum or relativistic claims set by hbar, often with c and N as well.
groups.rank_note: Ranked from fewest governing constants to most; hbar with c and N makes this group last.

groups.statement: Classical methods and models whose scale is set by particle number N and classical dynamics, with no role for ħ.
groups.rank_note: Classified by whether the scale is fixed by classical constants and N alone.

groups.statement: Models and structures of condensed matter whose scale involves ħ through quantum behavior or exact symmetry constraints.
groups.rank_note: Classified by whether ħ or symmetry structure enters the scale of the claim.
